# Persistent Structures & Structural Sharing

"Immutable" sounds expensive — surely changing one value means copying the whole structure? **No.** Persistent structures copy only the *path* from the root to the change and **share everything else** with the old version. Both versions stay fully usable forever.

The Clojure cell (ClojureScript, running in your browser) builds a binary search tree where every node carries a unique allocation id. Then it "inserts" a value, which really builds a *new* tree. Because the ids never lie, we can see exactly which nodes the two trees share — and the JS cell below draws it.

(require '[clojure.string :as str])

;; Every allocated node gets a unique id - that is our proof of sharing.
(def counter (atom 0))
(defn node [v l r] {:id (swap! counter inc) :val v :left l :right r})

;; Path copying: the branch we walk is rebuilt (new ids), the branch we
;; don't walk is REUSED (same map, same id).
(defn insert [t v]
  (cond
    (nil? t)       (node v nil nil)
    (< v (:val t)) (node (:val t) (insert (:left t) v) (:right t))
    (> v (:val t)) (node (:val t) (:left t) (insert (:right t) v))
    :else          t))

(defn build [vals] (reduce insert nil vals))

(defn collect [t]
  (when t
    (concat [{:id (:id t) :val (:val t)
              :left (when (:left t) (:id (:left t)))
              :right (when (:right t) (:id (:right t)))}]
            (collect (:left t))
            (collect (:right t)))))

(def tree-a (build [50 30 70 20 40 60 80 35 45]))
(def before @counter)
(def tree-b (insert tree-a 42))
(def allocated (- @counter before))

(def ids-a (set (map :id (collect tree-a))))
(def ids-b (set (map :id (collect tree-b))))
(def shared (count (filter ids-a ids-b)))

(println "tree A:" (count ids-a) "nodes")
(println "insert 42 allocated only" allocated "new nodes (the root-to-leaf path)")
(println "tree B:" (count ids-b) "nodes," shared "of them SHARED with tree A")
(println "tree A still intact:" (count (collect tree-a)) "nodes, untouched")

(defn node-json [n]
  (format "{\"id\":%d,\"val\":%d,\"left\":%s,\"right\":%s}"
          (:id n) (:val n)
          (or (:left n) "null") (or (:right n) "null")))
(defn tree-json [t]
  (str "{\"root\":" (:id t) ",\"nodes\":["
       (str/join "," (map node-json (collect t))) "]}"))

(println (str "__NB_SET__ {\"key\":\"pbst\",\"value\":{\"a\":" (tree-json tree-a)
              ",\"b\":" (tree-json tree-b) "}}"))

## Seeing the sharing

The JS cell renders both trees as SVG. **Grey nodes appear in both trees — they are literally the same objects.** Only the amber path (plus the new leaf) was allocated by the insert.

## This is how Clojure's own collections work

The toy BST copies an O(log n) path per update. Clojure's built-in vectors and maps do exactly the same trick on 32-way trees, so the path is ~log₃₂ n — 4 hops for a million entries:

;; The built-ins do the same trick at scale. One assoc into a 100k-entry
;; vector reuses almost everything - including the untouched tail objects.
(def big (vec (range 100000)))

;; A clock in nanoseconds: the JVM has one built in, the browser counts in milliseconds.
(defn now-ns [] #?(:clj (System/nanoTime) :cljs (* 1e6 (js/performance.now))))

(def t0 (now-ns))
(def big2 (assoc big 50000 :changed))
(def micros (/ (- (now-ns) t0) 1000.0))

(println (format "assoc into 100k-entry vector: %.1f microseconds" micros))
(println "original untouched:" (= 50000 (big 50000)))
(println "new version changed:" (= :changed (big2 50000)))
;; identical? is Java ==, pointer equality: the last element of both
;; vectors is the very same object.
(println "tail object shared:  " (identical? (peek big) (peek big2)))

## Try this

- Insert `65` instead of `42` in the first Clojure cell — the copied path runs down the *right* side; count the amber nodes.
- Insert a value already present (`40`) — path copying short-circuits: **zero** new nodes; the drawing shows two identical grey trees.
- Chain three inserts (`(-> tree-a (insert 42) (insert 5) (insert 99))`) and check how the allocation count grows — still O(log n) each.
- In the JS cell, colour nodes by *how many* trees reference them, keeping every intermediate version of the chained insert.
